1755-lisbon-earthquake.s: The 1755 Lisbon earthquake was a catastrophic earthquake, followed by a tsunami and fires, that destroyed much of the Portuguese capital in 1755. It killed tens of thousands of people and devastated the city's buildings, archives and commercial wealth.

1931-constitution-of-ethiopia.s: The 1931 Constitution of Ethiopia was the first written constitution of the Ethiopian Empire, promulgated by Emperor Haile Selassie in 1931. It created a bicameral parliament with limited powers while confirming the emperor's supreme authority and the dynasty's claim to rule.

4-2-kiloyear-event.s: The 4.2-kiloyear event was a period of severe aridification and climatic disruption around 2200–2150 BCE that affected much of the Near East and other regions. Reduced rainfall undermined rain-fed agriculture in northern Mesopotamia and contributed to population movements and…

5th-dalai-lama.s: The 5th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Lobsang Gyatso, was the first Dalai Lama to hold political power over all Tibet. In 1642 his patron Güshi Khan of the Khoshut Mongols defeated the Tsangpa kings and handed him authority, founding the Ganden Phodrang government.

14th-dalai-lama.s: The 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, was born in Amdo and recognised as the reincarnation of the Thirteenth Dalai Lama, being enthroned in Lhasa in 1940. He took full power in 1950 as the People's Liberation Army invaded Tibet.

19th-route-army.s: The 19th Route Army was a Chinese Nationalist army from Guangdong that won fame defending Shanghai against Japan in the January 28 Incident of 1932. Moved to Fujian, its commanders rebelled in 1933 against Chiang Kai-shek's policy of appeasing Japan and set up the Fujian…

2018-armenian-revolution.s: The 2018 Armenian revolution, also called the Velvet Revolution, was a wave of peaceful protests in Armenia in April and May 2018. It began against Serzh Sargsyan's move from president to prime minister under a new parliamentary constitution and forced his resignation within a…

1988-armenian-earthquake.s: The 1988 Armenian earthquake struck northern Soviet Armenia on 7 December 1988 with a magnitude of about 6.8, destroying the town of Spitak and heavily damaging Leninakan, now Gyumri. At least 25,000 people were killed and hundreds of thousands left homeless.

26-baku-commissars.s: The 26 Baku Commissars were Bolshevik and Left Socialist Revolutionary leaders of the Baku Commune, among them Stepan Shaumian, who governed Baku in 1918. 2006-peoples-movement.s: The 2006 People's Movement, also called Jana Andolan II, was a wave of general strikes and mass protests in Nepal in April 2006 against the direct rule of King Gyanendra. 2004-summer-olympics.s: The 2004 Summer Olympics were held in Athens from 13 to 29 August 2004, bringing the Games back to the city of the first modern Olympics of 1896. More than 10,000 athletes from 201 national Olympic committees took part.

1527-election-in-cetin.s: The election in Cetin was the assembly of Croatian nobles held at Cetin Castle on 1 January 1527, after King Louis II died at Mohács. 1992-summer-olympics.s: The 1992 Summer Olympics were held in Barcelona, Spain, from 25 July to 9 August 1992. The first Games after the end of the Cold War without a major boycott, they included a Unified Team of former Soviet republics and a reunited Germany, and South Africa returned after decades…

1st-czechoslovak-army-corps.s: The 1st Czechoslovak Army Corps was a Czechoslovak formation that fought alongside the Red Army in the Second World War, formed in 1944 from the brigade raised in the Soviet Union under Ludvík Svoboda. It suffered heavy losses in the Battle of the Dukla Pass in autumn 1944 and…

1693-sicily-earthquake.s: The 1693 Sicily earthquake struck south-eastern Sicily on 11 January 1693, after a foreshock two days earlier, and is the most destructive in Italian history. It killed about 60,000 people and destroyed Catania, Noto, Ragusa and dozens of other towns of the Val di Noto.

1936-summer-olympics.s: The 1936 Summer Olympics were held in Berlin in August 1936. The Nazi regime used them as a propaganda showcase, temporarily toning down open anti-Jewish measures, and introduced the torch relay from Olympia.

2011-christchurch-earthquake.s: The 2011 Christchurch earthquake was a magnitude 6.2 earthquake that struck Christchurch, New Zealand, on 22 February 2011. 2008-summer-olympics.s: The 2008 Summer Olympics were held in Beijing from 8 to 24 August 2008, the first Olympic Games hosted by China. 1989-tiananmen-square-protests-and-massa.s: The 1989 Tiananmen Square protests were student-led demonstrations in Beijing and other Chinese cities from April to June 1989, calling for political reform, freedom of the press and an end to corruption. 27th-jager-battalion.s: The 27th Jäger Battalion was a unit of Finnish volunteers trained in Germany during the First World War, when Finland was still a grand duchy of the Russian Empire. 1954-guatemalan-coup-detat.s: The 1954 Guatemalan coup d'état overthrew the elected president Jacobo Árbenz, whose land reform had expropriated unused land of the United Fruit Company. 1st-proletarian-brigade.s: The 1st Proletarian Brigade was the first regular brigade of the Yugoslav Partisans, formed on 21 December 1941 at Rudo in eastern Bosnia from units that had retreated from the Republic of Užice. Its formation marked the shift from local guerrilla detachments to a mobile army.

2nd-king-edward-viis-own-gurkha-rifles.n: 2nd King Edward VII's Own Gurkha Rifles

1383-1385-portuguese-interregnum.s: The 1383–1385 Portuguese interregnum was a succession crisis and civil war in Portugal after the death of King Ferdinand I without a male heir.
